items.item_text: Basic Life Support - CPR, upon hire and
1 year acute hospital imaging procedures

Technologist will perform quality procedures and radiographs using the appropriate department routine. Must be able to perform all examinations using all the general radiographic equipment including portables and OR radiographic equipment. Selects and uses proper immobilization and supportive devices when necessary.

Demonstrates knowledge of the different views associated with each exam. Uses the correct markers and labels all films correctly. Must mark and label exams correctly. Ensures initials are on all images. Responsible to make sure all exams display the patient name.

Prepares the room, equipment and supplies as dictated by the particular examination or patient need. By end of shift room assignment must be stocked and cleaned. Responsible to call for service if equipment is down and unable to reach Supervisor.

Responsible to let the Supervisor know when they are getting low on a particular supply. Verifies correct patient using two patient identifiers. Follows standard patient identifier of name and date of birth. Evaluates patient condition to see if they are capable of answering questions necessary for proper identification.

Involves patient family members when needed for proper identification. Demonstrates awareness of radiation safety for patients, self and co-workers. Will not exceed radiation exposure limit for calendar year as stated in Title 17. Must demonstrate on images that correct shielding was used on the patients. Responsible to check the Radiation Film Badge report.

Exhibits and demonstrates good communication skills with patients, family members, co-workers and hospital staff. No negative feed-back. Ensures patient or family member understands procedure. Adopts AIDET program to ensure quality patient care. Responsible that images reflect ability to compensate for age of the patient.
